nota: Words of this language that look borrowed from another language but do not exist there with that meaning, grouped by the language they imitate.

parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from aerobics. While aerobic exists in English to refer to aerobics, it is an adjective and not a noun.

From beamen (“to beam; to project”) + -er; the former from English beam (“to transmit matter or information via a high-tech wireless mechanism”). Inasmuch as the English verb does not share the figura

Seemingly a pseudo-anglicism, potentially on the basis of bis zum Gehtnichtmehr, with the first part a mistranslation of geht, but the earliest written attestations already lack an equivalent to mehr.
Borrowed from French body, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English bodysuit.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from body + bag. The English term body bag refers to a bag designed to contain a human corpse; the German term for that is Leichensack.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from break + ball. Compare Czech brejkbol, Norwegian Bokmål breakball, and Slovak brejkbal.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from candy + storm, after Shitstorm.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from casting + show.
Borrowed from English catcher. The sense "professional wrestler" is a pseudo-anglicism derived from catch-as-catch-can + -er; compare French catcheur and Serbo-Croatian kečer.

parole.significato: city center, downtown, central business district
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from city. The feminine gender is likely an analogy to Stadt.

parole.significato: you don't dip your pen in company ink
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from don't + fuck + in + the + factory. The expression is not found in English texts and is unknown in the English-speaking world.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from Dress + English man.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from Latin ego (“I”) + shooter.
Compound of Ende + Boss. Pseudo-anglicism, derived from end boss.

From English flipper (“lever in a pinball machine used to strike the ball”). The senses "pinball" and "pinball machine" are a pseudo-anglicism, with "flipper" being used in many languages to refer the
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from Flipper + -ern.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from photo shoot + -ing.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from future. The masculine gender is likely inherited from Futures-Kontrakt.

parole.significato: A box in a public place in which people can put unwanted objects for other people to take; a dropbox.
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from give + box.

parole.significato: barbecue (social gathering at which food is grilled and consumed)
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from grill + party. Compare Danish, Norwegian, and Swedish grillparty.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from happy ending.

parole.significato: High society, posh people, especially those with snobbish attitudes.
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, from English high society and Snob (itself from English snob).
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from home + trainer. Compare Dutch hometrainer.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from lost + place.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from match ball. Compare Czech mečbol, Norwegian Bokmål matchball, Polish meczbol, and Slovak mečbal.

parole.parola: my English is not the yellow from the egg, but it goes
parole.significato: Used to apologize for or acknowledge poor English skills.
parole.testo: Hyperliteral translation (Denglisch) of German mein Englisch ist nicht das Gelbe vom Ei, aber es geht (“my English is not the best, but it's alright”).
parole.chiave_albero: my English is not the yellow from the egg, but it goes|1

parole.significato: if it ain't broke, don't fix it; leave well enough alone
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, possibly from the field of computing, although this origin is disputed.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from open end.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from open end.

parole.significato: A public showing of a sports match or other event on a large television screen.
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from public + viewing.
Pseudo-anglicism, analogous to Pullover.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from shooting.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from show + master, equivalent to Show + Master.
Borrowed from French smoking, and this a pseudo-anglicism, derived from an ellipsis of English smoking jacket.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from spleen.

parole.significato: synonym of das Gelbe vom Ei
parole.testo: Back-formation from my English is not the yellow from the egg, but it goes.

From English tramp, from Middle English trampen (“to walk heavily”), from Middle Low German trampen (“to stamp”) (trampeln (“to walk with heavy steps”), see English trample) or from Middle Dutch tramp
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from English tramper or trampen + -er.
Pseudo-anglicism, derived from wall + box.

parole.significato: wholecar (a piece of graffiti that covers an entire train carriage)
parole.testo: Pseudo-anglicism, derived from whole + car.
Pseudo-Latinism, coined from Latin botulus (“sausage”) with the addition of the Latinate suffix -ismus.
19th c. Pseudo-Latinism, possibly from French fécal + Latin -ālie, from Middle French fecal, from Latin faex.
Borrowed from English hocus-pocus, and this a pseudo-Latinism; see that entry for more.
Pseudo-Latinism, derived from German Joke m + Latin -us, or directly from Latin iocus.

Pseudo-Latinism, derived from Lappen (“cloth, rag”) + Latin -ālia (neuter plural of relational adjective suffix), 17th c.. Initially as the plural Lappalia, then showing the Germanized plural Lappalie

parole.significato: tumult; riot (loud and unrestrained behaviour by one or more people, often with property damage, sometimes also bodily…
parole.testo: Originally plural of now obsolete Randal (“noise, tumult”). Pseudo-Latinism, derived from a humorous pseudo-Latin formation from dialectal Rand (“noise, ballyhoo”) to rhyme with Skandal (“scandal”) an
Pseudo-Latinism, derived from Low German sammelsūr/Sammelsūr (“[sour] dish made from various leftovers”) + Latin -ium.

parole.significato: the voice of the people is worth nothing
parole.testo: Pseudo-Latinism, literally "the voice of the people [is] the voice of a cow", with a humorously rhyming but grammatically incorrect genitive bovi instead of bovis.
Since 1917. Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from bon + confort + -euse or bon + fort + -euse or bonne + force + -euse.
Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from fad + -esse.
Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from piquant + -erie.
Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from English rummy + French -é.
From Saison + -al. A pseudo-Gallicism, perhaps modeled on English seasonal (compare French saisonnier).
Pseudo-Gallicism, derived from Suite + -ier.

parole.significato: talmi, an alloy of mostly zinc and copper and occasionally some tin and lead and about a percent of gold used for jewel…
parole.testo: Pseudo-Gallicism created as a trade name in Austria or Bavaria.
Pseudo-Italianism for leck mich (literally “lick me”) functioning as a minced oath.

parole.significato: spick-and-span; shipshape (in very good state, especially in terms of cleanliness)
parole.testo: Pseudo-Italianism; humorous alteration of piekfein with fein replaced by Italian bello.
Borrowed from English hentai, and this a pseudo-Japonism derived from Japanese 変態(へんたい) (hentai); see that entry for more.
